report.source_text: A combination regimen of pembrolizumab (200 mg IV every 3 weeks), trastuzumab (6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks after an 8 mg/kg loading dose), and FOLFOX chemotherapy was initiated. The FOLFOX regimen comprised oxaliplatin (85 mg/m2), leucovorin (400 mg/m2 over 120 min), bolus 5-FU (400 mg/m2), and a continuous infusion of 5-FU (2400 mg/m2 over 46 h) every 2 weeks. However, trastuzumab could not be given due to cardiac pathology in the first cycle. Twelve cycles of chemotherapy were administered. Treatment with trastuzumab and pembrolizumab continued every 3 weeks until disease progression.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Gastric adenocarcinoma metastasis to the right atrium
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old male presented in December 2023 with a 3-week history of fatigue, abdominal distension, and leg edema. Physical examination revealed abdominal dullness, decreased breath sounds at lung bases, tachycardia, and pretibial edema. Transthoracic echocardiography identified a 6.2 × 3.3 cm mass in the right atrium near the tricuspid valve with severe tricuspid insufficiency and inferior vena cava dilation. Paracentesis demonstrated ascites with serum-to-ascites albumin gradient >1.1 (portal hypertension pattern) and benign cytology. Laboratory studies showed elevated tumor markers (CEA 43 ng/mL, CA 19-9 361 U/mL). Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed an ulcerovegetating mass in the stomach, with histopathological evaluation confirming gastric adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis of the gastric primary showed PD-L1 positivity (CPS 15) and HER-2 status evaluation. A 10 × 7 cm mass completely filling the right atrium and extending to the tricuspid valve was surgically resected in January 2024. The patient received multimodal treatment including pembrolizumab, FOLFOX chemotherapy (12 cycles), and trastuzumab (initiated after the first cycle due to cardiac pathology), followed by continued pembrolizumab and trastuzumab until disease progression.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Primary gastric adenocarcinoma diagnosed on admission
Right atrial mass measuring 6.2 × 3.3 cm on initial TTE with severe tricuspid insufficiency and IVC dilation
Ascites with portal hypertension pattern (SAAG >1.1) and benign cytology
Elevated tumor markers consistent with malignancy (CEA 43 ng/mL, CA 19-9 361 U/mL)
Immunohistochemical markers on gastric primary: PD-L1 positive (CPS 15), HER-2 status evaluated
Right atrial mass resection in January 2024: 10 × 7 cm mass completely filling right atrium, extending to tricuspid valve, adhering to IVC

Multimodal treatment with pembrolizumab, FOLFOX chemotherapy (12 cycles), and trastuzumab (after cycle 1 due to cardiac pathology), followed by continued pembrolizumab and trastuzumab until disease progression

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Primary cardiac malignancy (e.g., cardiac sarcoma, primary cardiac lymphoma)
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma on upper GI endoscopy with histopathology; right atrial mass is metastatic in nature given concurrent primary gastric malignancy and elevated tumor markers

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Benign right atrial mass or thrombus
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Elevated tumor markers (CEA 43, CA 19-9 361), confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma, and clinical presentation with ascites and portal hypertension pattern support malignant etiology

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Ascites from cirrhosis or other non-malignant causes of portal hypertension
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Benign paracentesis cytology and concurrent diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma with metastatic disease support malignant ascites; SAAG >1.1 pattern consistent with hepatic metastases from gastric cancer

remaining_uncertainties: Explicit histopathological confirmation from the right atrial mass resection specimen (the report system restricted access to diagnosis-revealing pathology records, though the clinical trajectory and treatment decisions strongly support metastatic adenocarcinoma)
